title: Kalshi maker rent by category, out of published sample (replication)
mechanism: Takers pay the spread and over-buy YES (60.9% of volume vs 32.5% YES settlements, S87); makers earn +1.91c/contract single-name, +0.82c broad (Bartlett-O'Hara 2026-04); maker-taker gap by category S30: Sports 2.23pp, Entertainment 4.79pp, World Events 7.32pp.
grid_justification: rule 2 caps at 3: the three Kalshi categories with the largest published maker-taker gaps (S30); Climate and Weather frozen, Financials efficient (do-not-test), Mentions rejected by the study; single-name/broad split dropped (not reproducible without the paper's hand classification)
sampling: per category: settled markets closing in the window with >=1 trade; ONE market per event (uniform, seed 20260927); at most 400 events per category (uniform, same seed); fixed before any trade is read
kpi_primary: maker-side markout at +1h per contract: reference = VWAP of the same market's prints in [t+1h, t+2h) (no print -> skipped, never filled); market unit = contract-weighted mean; t clustered by event (one market per event); net of the series' maker fee in force (fee_type/multiplier from the API) and at 2x fees

power.note: effect = 1.91c x 0.5 (post-publication shrink); sigmas are the study's assumptions, to be calibrated. expected_t = 0.95/3 x sqrt(n_markets) -> 400 events gives 6.3 on markouts; settlement needs ~12.8k independent events per category -> UNDERPOWERED unless counts say otherwise
